name: Okta: pull security events
description: Every 5 minutes, reads security-relevant Okta System Log events (ThreatInsight, breached credentials, session roaming, lockouts, user-reported suspicious activity, admin privilege grants, denied pushes, MFA bypass attempts, app sign-on policy denials) and creates one pending alert per event.

params.label: Okta domain
params.help: Your Okta org host name, without https://. A custom domain works too.

secrets.name: OKTA_API_TOKEN
secrets.description: Okta API token created by a Read-Only Administrator (sent as `Authorization: SSWS <token>`).

setup:
### Okta side
1. Create (or pick) a dedicated Okta admin account and give it the **Read-Only Administrator** role (Security > Administrators). An API token has exactly the permissions of the admin who created it, and Read-Only Administrator can view the System Log.
2. Signed in as that admin: Security > API > Tokens > **Create token**. Copy the value once.
3. Optional: under the token, restrict it to the network zone of this server.

### Here
1. Settings > Secrets: add `OKTA_API_TOKEN` with allowed host = your Okta domain.
2. Install with `OKTA_DOMAIN` = `acme.okta.com` (no scheme), review, then enable.

### What it calls
`GET https://<OKTA_DOMAIN>/api/v1/logs?since=<previous run>&sortOrder=ASCENDING&limit=200&filter=<eventType list>` (a polling request: no `until`, ascending). Each event becomes an alert with source `okta`, external id = the event `uuid`, title = `displayMessage (actor.alternateId)`, severity mapped from the event `severity`: ERROR → high, WARN → medium, INFO → low, DEBUG → info. Re-reading an event (overlapping windows) does not create a second alert.

In Okta Identity Engine a rejected push is usually logged as `user.authentication.auth_via_mfa` with outcome reason `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, which is too noisy to pull blindly; add it to the filter in the HTTP step if you want it.

### Limits
ponytail: one page per run (`limit=200`, Okta allows up to 1000); the `Link: rel="next"` header is not followed, so more than 200 matching events in 5 minutes are cut off. Raise `limit` and the loop's `max_items` (max 500) together if you hit it. A non-200 answer (bad token, 429) creates nothing and fails the run with the HTTP status; the next run re-reads the window from the last successful run (at most 24 h back). Okta keeps System Log events for 90 days and rate-limits `/api/v1/logs` per org.

Docs: [List System Log events](https://developer.okta.com/docs/api/openapi/okta-management/management/tag/SystemLog/#tag/SystemLog/operation/listLogEvents), [System Log query](https://developer.okta.com/docs/reference/system-log-query/), [Event types](https://developer.okta.com/docs/reference/api/event-types/), [Admin roles](https://help.okta.com/oie/en-us/Content/Topics/Security/administrators-admin-comparison.htm), [Rate limits](https://developer.okta.com/docs/reference/rl-global-mgmt/).

config.url: https://%%OKTA_DOMAIN%%/api/v1/logs?since={{ trigger.since | urlencode }}&sortOrder=ASCENDING&limit=200&filter={{ 'eventType eq "security.threat.detected" or eventType eq "security.breached_credential.detected" or eventType eq "security.session.detect_client_roaming" or eventType eq "user.account.lock" or eventType eq "user.account.lock.limit" or eventType eq "user.account.report_suspicious_activity_by_enduser" or eventType eq "user.account.privilege.grant" or eventType eq "user.mfa.okta_verify.deny_push" or eventType eq "user.mfa.attempt_bypass" or eventType eq "application.policy.sign_on.deny_access"' | urlencode }}

config.title: {{ loop.item.displayMessage or loop.item.eventType }} ({{ (loop.item.actor or {}).get('alternateId') or 'unknown actor' }})
